features.title: Vitest runs as a test-results card
features.summary: A bash call whose output carries a Vitest summary renders as a test-results card instead of a terminal block: a pass/fail/skip bar, All/Failed/Skipped/Slow filters, one row per test file, and for each failing test its assertion diff, source location, code frame, Ask to fix, Rerun and Copy. While a Vitest command runs the card shows a running state; any other command keeps the native bash card.

configuration.constraints: Boolean; show a Vitest run as a test-results card instead of the terminal output.
Boolean; show a running test card while a Vitest command runs.
Boolean; offer Ask to fix and Rerun on failing tests.
Boolean; open the card and its failing files and tests when the run settles.

failureModes: The Host streams no shell output while a call runs, so the running state cannot count finished tests.
Vitest's default reporter prints only files with failures; passing files show as a count and their tests stay hidden unless the run used --reporter=verbose.
Ask to fix and Rerun appear only while a Composer provider runs; Copy is always available.
Output from another runner, a spilled preview or a persistent shell keeps the native bash card.

features.title: Stack traces under failed commands
features.summary: A bash call that is not a Vitest run but printed an error with a stack trace (Node, Deno, Bun, JVM or Python) keeps its native card and gains a Stack trace card under it: the error headline, your frames innermost first with library frames one toggle away, and each frame opening its file at its line.
features.currentSurface: transcript: Stack trace card under a bash call

configuration.constraints: Boolean; add a stack trace card under a command whose output holds one.

failureModes: Only the first trace in the output is read; a Caused by chain ends it.
A single frame-like line with no error header above it is not taken for a crash.
Frames open through the Host file opener; a path outside the workspace may not open.
